scope: Context-aware mixed-font fallback inside logical script/bidi/style items, observed cluster and unsafe-to-break constraints, full-context boundary reshaping, candidate batching and canonical effective style keys. Paragraph preparation only; not width-based line fitting, baseline geometry, painting, complete Emoji policy or Office/WPS certification.
artifactSizeScope: Incomplete development CLI/worker and Rust/C++ WASM artifacts only. Full rendering/media/fonts/host distribution and installer sizes are not measured here.

itemization.filter: kind=itemization; the other 34 paragraph responses in this report intentionally use the new contract

benchmark.scope: Warm in-memory Node/WASM paragraph preparation with identical input, algorithm and byte-identical results; only the C++ component upload batching differs. Excludes file I/O, component creation, cold start, width fitting, geometry, painting, worker scheduling and the desktop host. Not a full-product performance claim.

work.individual: Transport proxy splits every component batch into single-run frames; Rust font verification, itemization, probes and boundary reshapes are unchanged.
work.batched: Production adapter uploads each candidate font once per batch; both modes still construct C++ face/font for every run.

benchmark.garbageCollection: Explicit GC before each sample, outside the timed interval. No font-result or cross-request verification cache.

contractChange.response: paragraph-shape-response replaces cascade with fallback, including logical fragments, whole-item probes, protected boundaries, reshape rejections and separate run/call counters. Profile unicode18-auto-items-hb14.5-mixed-font-reshape-v2. Unreleased development contract change.

limitations: Font assignment preserves extended graphemes and takes a conservative union of dependencies observed in candidate probes. It is an explicit implementation policy, not a Unicode line breaking algorithm or complete target-application typography policy.

Partial selections are always freshly reshaped with logical context; probe glyph arrays are never sliced into final fragments. The unsafe-to-concat flag is not treated as a prohibition on font switching or as a one-sided guarantee for glyph splicing.

Rejection after boundary reshaping excludes the candidate for the whole attempted fragment. Conservative region union and rejection can leave text unresolved even where a more advanced policy might find another valid segmentation.

cmap-14 based variation checks remain conservative. GSUB-only variants and general Emoji/ZWJ presentation are not certified by absence of .notdef; selected actual fixtures do not establish complete Emoji support.

Language tag case, independent axis order and identical digest/face aliases normalize only computation keys. All raw styles/resources are still checked. Styles inside an extended grapheme remain unsupported by this paragraph interface.
Native/WASM and upstream numeric matching do not certify glyph outlines, rasterization, family aesthetics, Office/WPS editability or final visual quality.
Width fitting, automatic line breaks, actual line-specific L1/L2 and boundary reshaping, mixed-font baseline metrics, paragraph/page geometry and vertical layout remain incomplete.

Actual C++ allocation failure is tested at first boundary reshape after successful probes; this is not an all-allocation-position fault campaign. Boundary-induced new missing glyph fallback is separately covered by a simulated backend.

The performance comparison varies only transport batching for byte-identical output. Warm in-memory Node timings exclude cold start, I/O, host scheduling, rendering and full product latency; cumulative uploads are not peak memory or installer size.
Native hard termination and WASM Worker cancellation, production resource accounting, FontManifest/target profiles, advanced presentation objects and Musterwork replacement gates remain incomplete.
